True happiness may not be found *only* through work—but perhaps it is found *through* work, when work is meaningful, just, and aligned with our values.

Happiness, then, is not a product of labor alone, but of a life lived with intention, dignity, and connection to something greater than oneself.

The statement “Only through work can one become truly happy” captures a vital insight but fails as a universal truth. While meaningful work is a powerful path to fulfillment, happiness arises from a constellation of human experiences—relationships, rest, creativity, and purpose. To equate happiness solely with work risks neglecting the full spectrum of what makes life meaningful. A more humane and balanced understanding honors both the dignity of work and the inherent worth of being—beyond the labor market.
